During the French colonial period, it was known as rue des Étoffes, also called Hang Vai Nau (Brown Cloth Street). In the past, Hang Vai Street was divided into two sections: the eastern segment was named Hang Vai, while the western part was called Hang Cuoc because residents there produced hoe blades and plow blades.

The predominant fabrics sold here were small-width dyed brown and dark-colored cloths. To distinguish it from another Hang Vai Street near Dong Thanh market (now the middle section of Thuoc Bac Street), which sells undyed small-width cloths, this street was specifically called Hang Vai Tham (Dark Cloth Street).
